Subject: Question on stale KV sessions / holdback credits

Hi Karthik —

Quick one from our engineering/finance team after the usage export: we see a non-trivial portion of token billing tied to long-lived sessions where the KV cache stayed warm but the user never resumed the flow (sessions flagged in our logs as "stale-inflight"). Our internal team calls these "holdback" cases — short-lived bursts that left KV behind for minutes -> hours.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide guidance/precedent on granting pilot credits for this pattern (we're seeing ~2.7% of billed tokens from these flows)?
- How does rounding/minimum unit logic apply when a session gets resurrected across billing windows? Example: first window counted 0.4 of a minimum unit and then later a resume pushes it >1.0 — do you retroactively rebalance?

Attaching a small CSV extract and a sample invoice diff for reference. Any quick guidance would help our reconciliation.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform
Ferry.ai

Alex —

Thanks for the samples, very helpful. High-level answers below so your finance team has something to work with before we loop in billing: 

1) Pilot credits: we typically approve small, time-boxed credits for pilots where engineering patterns cause charged-but-unused KV state. For a 2–3% hit we’d propose a one-time credit equal to the observed excess for the pilot month, capped (we usually cap at 25% of the monthly invoice for pilot credits). Grace and Marissa, does that cap sound right for this type of customer?

2) Rounding/retroactive balancing: our current meter works per-billing-window and does not do retroactive rebalance across closed invoices. Practically that means: if a session accrues 0.4 units in window A and then later in window B resumes and pushes it to 1.2 aggregated, window A already billed 0.4 (rounded up to the billing quantum as applicable) — we do not go back and adjust. That said, we can offer a reconciliation credit when the pattern is demonstrably caused by SDK behavior we flagged as a bug or by our rollouts.

3) Suggested operational mitigations: prefix eviction TTLs on KV, heartbeat trimming on inactive sessions, or a small SDK change to commit KV only after X tokens. We can share engineering notes if helpful.

If you want, I can propose a one-time credit to make the month whole and follow with a short-term tech fix/telemetry change to avoid recurrence.

-Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
